sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Maines were minor Irish heroes. They were the seven identically named sons of queen Medb of Connacht and king Ailill mac Máta. A legend says Medb wished for the death of her enemy, king Concobar mac Nessa of Ulster. A druid prophesied that her son Maine would kill him. Medb had no sons of that name, so she renamed them all. One of the Maines, first called Sin and later Maine Mórghor, went with a band of warriors to Ulster to court the maiden Fearbh, daughter of Gearg. A sudden wind blew up, which Maine's druid warned was a bad omen. A woman of the Otherworld appeared to Concobar and led him to Gearg's home. There the host and Maine Mórghor were slain. Medb had a vision of the events but arrived too late to save her son. Another hero of the same name was a Norse prince who served king Concobar. When the errant hero Noísiu returned to Ireland with the doomed Deirdre, Noísiu fell to Maine's sword.
